place.why: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh; address in Edinburgh EH11

summary: At the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, your complaint starts with NHS Lothian, usually within 6 months of the event or of realising there is a reason to complain, and NHS Lothian has an online feedback/complaint form. If you are still unhappy after NHS Lothian’s final response, the independent next stage is the SPSO, usually within 12 months of when you knew about the problem. For compensation in Scotland, the verified route is a medical-negligence damages claim; legal aid may cover medical negligence, and Scotland also allows capped no-win-no-fee success fee agreements.

steps.what: The Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh is an NHS Lothian hospital, so this was public NHS care. NHS Lothian's patient-facing material describes a two-stage complaints process for patients, with SPSO as the external review route if you stay unhappy.
steps.deadline: "Normally, you must make your complaint within six months of:" ... "12 months after the event itself."
points: The deadline wording NHS Lothian gives is: complaint within six months of the event or of finding out you have a reason to complain, and no longer than 12 months after the event itself.
The leaflet says: "At the investigation stage, staff will write to you within three working days to acknowledge your complaint."
The leaflet also says: "Staff will write to you with a full response within 20 working days of receiving your complaint at the investigation stage."
The online form "cannot be saved so must be completed and submitted in one go."
When submitted, the form goes to the "Patient Experience Team for response."
steps.appliesIf: Public NHS care at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh / NHS Lothian.
alternatives: NHS Lothian's leaflet says you can complain by phone, email, online, or by letter.
missing: Which department/ward saw you in A&E
Exact date of the first attendance and later rediscovery

steps.what: If NHS Lothian's final complaint response is not good enough, the next independent stage is the Scottish Public Services Ombudsman. SPSO says you normally need to complete the organisation's complaints process first, and it offers an online complaint-checker route.
steps.deadline: "We do not normally investigate complaints if you have known about the problem for more than 12 months before complaining."
points: SPSO is "the final stage for complaints about most public services in Scotland."
SPSO says: "Once you have the final decision from the organisation, if you are still not happy, you can then bring your complaint to us."
SPSO normally will not investigate if you have known about the problem for more than 12 months before complaining.
The online route starts with the "Complaint checker" asking, "Is your complaint about a Scottish public service?"
requires: NHS Lothian's final decision / completion of the provider's complaints process
steps.appliesIf: You have already complained to NHS Lothian and remain unhappy with its final response.
missing: When NHS Lothian gave its final complaint response

steps.what: For compensation for negligent NHS care in Scotland, the route I could verify is legal action for damages, not an NHS complaints payout. PASS says legal action is needed for financial compensation, and if you start legal action while complaining, the NHS complaints process stops.
steps.deadline: "no action to which this section applies shall be brought unless it is commenced within a period of 3 years after—"
points: PASS says: "Legal action is needed if you want financial compensation for medical negligence."
PASS says: "If you take legal action whilst you are making a complaint through the NHS complaints process, the NHS will immediately stop the complaints process."
The usual Scottish personal injury time limit is 3 years, running from the injury date or the later date when the pursuer became aware of key facts.
Scottish Courts say the National Personal Injury Court procedures are available throughout Scotland, including to people acting on their own behalf.
In this run I found a Scottish Government consultation on a proposed "No-blame" scheme, but not a current live patient scheme page.
requires: Usually instructing a specialist clinical negligence solicitor if you want to pursue damages
steps.appliesIf: A patient wants financial compensation for harm from clinical treatment in Scotland.
alternatives: NHS complaint for explanation/apology/service improvement, but PASS says the complaints route is not the compensation route.
missing: Your exact date of birth, because limitation rules differ for children
The date you first knew the fracture had been missed and had caused lasting harm
Whether any private treatment is involved

steps.what: Civil legal aid in Scotland can cover medical negligence cases, subject to eligibility, and SLAB provides official online estimators for both civil legal aid and early advice and assistance. Scotland also allows success fee agreements, which legislation describes as types of "no win, no fee" agreements, with capped percentages on personal-injury damages.
points: mygov.scot lists "trying to get compensation for injuries after an accident or for medical negligence" as a civil legal aid example.
SLAB's civil legal aid checker says: "This estimator helps you work out if you are likely to qualify financially for civil legal aid."
SLAB also offers an "Advice and assistance" estimator for early legal advice.
Scottish legislation says success fee agreements include types of "no win, no fee" agreements.
For personal injury or death claims, the regulation gives three tiers: 20% on the first £100,000, 10% on the amount over £100,000 but not exceeding £500,000, and 2.5% on the amount over £500,000.
requires: Financial eligibility and, for civil legal aid, merits/solicitor assessment
steps.appliesIf: An adult in Scotland needs help paying for a medical negligence claim or early legal advice.
alternatives: A private success fee agreement / speculative fee agreement with a solicitor.
missing: Your income, savings and any partner's finances for legal-aid checks
Whether you want only early advice or full court representation

steps.what: The official directory is the Law Society of Scotland's Find a Solicitor service. It lets you search by postcode or city/town, area of law, and whether the firm does legal aid work; PASS links directly to the Law Society search for medical negligence claimant firms.

It has fields for "Postcode or city/town" and "Area of Law".
It also has a "Legal aid ?" filter.
PASS links directly to the Law Society search using the medical-negligence claimant area-of-law code.

steps.body: Healthcare Improvement Scotland / Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN)
steps.what: The Scottish body I could verify for national clinical guidance is SIGN, which sits within Healthcare Improvement Scotland and develops guidelines with professionals and patients.
points: The official page names "Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN)".
Healthcare Improvement Scotland says: "We work with health and social care professionals and patients to develop guidelines."
steps.appliesIf: You want the Scottish guidance body whose guidelines clinicians use.

steps.what: PASS is the independent patient-help service for NHS Scotland complaints and concerns that I could verify. PASS says it supports NHS users to understand their rights, raise concerns, give feedback or make a complaint, and it offers a web contact form and an advice line.
points: PASS says: "Our trained advisers support anyone who uses NHS Scotland to understand their rights and responsibilities as a patient, raise concerns, give feedback, or make a complaint."
PASS says: "We are an independent service, delivered by the Citizens Advice network in Scotland."
PASS says: "please fill in your contact details on our simple web contact form, below."
PASS also says: "Call us on our Advice Line: 0800 917 2127 (Mon – Fri 9am – 5pm)."
steps.appliesIf: You want independent help with an NHS Scotland complaint or concern.
alternatives: You can complain directly to NHS Lothian or, after a final NHS response, to SPSO.

steps.what: NHS Lothian says you can request copies of health records through its online Request for Records Portal or by downloading a Subject Access Request form and sending it by email or post. The live portal is reachable, but it stops at a sign-in/create-account wall.

Another route is the "Downloadable Form:"
NHS Lothian says: "You can return your forms by email to Loth.sarteam@nhs.scot or by post to:"
